# `ios-virtual` operations

21 operations. Generated from `assets/operations.json`; [all references](index.md).

### ios.virtual.status

Virtual iOS device: status. read-only, idempotent.

Read whether a virtual iOS device profile is configured, its current run, phase, guest job and any start or stop that is in progress. A guest job started from another data directory has no guest_state here; that is unknown, not stopped. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. Also reports model (for the next start), running_model (of the current run), running_panel (the current run's panel as WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ:WIDTH_MMxHEIGHT_MM, as its guest job's request gave it to the engine, so a later edit of the profile does not change it; null when that boot named no panel. Without a guest job: the model's own panel, or the profile's display profile for the Home-button phone; null for an unknown recorded model), models (the choice: id, name, panel, and source apple or derived) and guest_ended when the guest has ended on its own since the last start, with guest_saved telling whether it flushed its storage and closed cleanly first (as a session does at its time limit). application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. applications lists the developer apps the profile names (bundle path, bundle_id); the start installs them from the guest-tools build that carries them. phase_started and phase_elapsed_seconds tell when the current phase began and how long it has run, and phases lists each phase of the current start or stop with its started time and seconds (empty for a state written before phases were logged). start_timing and stop_timing break the last start and stop down into steps with their seconds (start: checks, preparation, disk_copy with its method, guest_tools, boot_request, input_hashing with its bytes, launcher, boot, app_install, guest_settings, unlock_and_launch, display_check; stop: guest_exit, output_hashing, finalize), with total_seconds, slowest and run; a step whose times are unknown is folded into the next one, which lists it under includes; null before the first start that recorded them. copy_progress, only in the preparing phase, compares the bytes of the new disk copy with those of its base (bytes_done, bytes_total, percent) and names the preparation's step and disk; a reflinked copy is complete at once. start_disk says whether the next start's disk copy fits in the profile's installs: needed_bytes, free_bytes, reclaimable_bytes (older copies the start deletes first), reflink and enough, the check ios.virtual.start refuses with; the status writes nothing to find out, so on a filesystem that might clone files and lacks room for a full copy enough and reflink are null until a start probes it. start_disk.method is how that start makes its root disk (copy, overlay or flatten), and start_disks the profile's choice (copy or overlay). Null when the base's disks or the filesystem cannot be read. last_run says in plain words how the last finished run ended: verified, the launcher's outcome, a summary, each reason it was not verified (no exit code 0, incomplete storage hashes, no confirmed flush, the graphics memory guard) and a remedy; null before the first run that recorded it. next names what to call when a start or stop ended halfway, with action (resume, unlock_then_resume, stop, record_end, start_again or wait), call, arguments, resumes (true when the call goes on with the running guest without a new disk copy) and why; null when nothing is left halfway. host reports on every call the graphics card's memory (gpu: source guard, the running guest's last guard check, or sysfs, the card with the most memory; used_bytes, total_bytes, free_bytes, guard_limit_free_bytes, the eighth the graphics memory guard keeps, level ok, low under a quarter free or short under the guard's limit, and short_checks and guard_stopping from the guard; null when no card reports memory) and the host's pressure (pressure: Linux PSI full avg10 and avg60 for io and memory against the start's admission limits, blocked naming those over them, observed false without PSI). liveness, while the guest runs, says whether it still shows signs of life: state live, quiet (no new frame, console output or guest answer for stall_seconds; normal for a still screen), stalled (the guest service did not answer a probe and neither it nor the screen showed life for stall_seconds) or booting (not judged); last_seen with the newest frame's number, the console log's size and the guest's last answer, each with when it last changed; and for a stalled phone recovery, the typed calls to make in order: ios.emulator.guest restart_ui, then ios.virtual.stop. The status never acts on the phone itself; it remembers the signs in liveness.json in the guest job's run directory.

- `probe` boolean: Also ask the running guest service for its status, bounded to 10 seconds, so that liveness can tell a still screen from a guest that no longer answers. Changes…

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.status
```

### ios.virtual.host_check

Check this machine for the virtual iOS device. read-only, idempotent.

Check whether this machine can run the virtual iOS device, before any setup step or start: architecture (x86_64), CPU (logical processors, VT-x or AMD-V, AVX2), /dev/kvm for the disk-preparing helper, memory (fail under 12 GiB, warn under 16 GiB), free disk on the filesystem of directory (by default the configured profile's installs, needing 32 GiB for one start's disk copy, else the data directory, needing 100 GiB for the setup chain), Vulkan drivers and the card with the most graphics memory (fail under 8 GiB, warn under 16 GiB or when under an eighth is free), the helper support's APFS module against the running kernel, and passt for the guest network. Each entry in checks has check, status (pass, warn or fail), found, message and a remedy unless it passed; ready is false when any check fails. host has logical_cpus, physical_cores (one per package and core among the CPUs this process may use) and memory_total_bytes, and recommend compares the configured profile's boot settings with them: each entry names a setting (boot.host_cpu_policy: performance with at least two physical cores more than application processors, scheduler with fewer cores than processors; boot.translation_cache_mib: 1024 under 16 GiB of memory, 2048 from 32 GiB), its current and suggested value and the reason; empty when they suit the host or no profile is configured. Nothing is changed. Reads /proc, /sys, PATH and the filesystem only; starts and writes nothing. A pass means the machine meets what the device was measured with, not that it was qualified on it.

- `directory` string (non-empty): Absolute existing directory whose filesystem will hold the setup chain's outputs; checked against the 100 GiB the chain needs
- `support` string (non-empty): Absolute helper support directory (prepare_ios_emulator.py output); by default the profile's, else the checkout's .tooling/ios-sptm/support

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.host_check
```

### ios.virtual.doctor

Check the virtual iOS device. read-only, idempotent.

One pass, warn or fail report on whether the configured virtual iOS device can start and how its last run ended, each item with a remedy: profile (profile.json and state.json readable), profile_inputs (every input profile.json names, checked as tools/ios_virtual_profile.py checks a new profile: engine, guest-control backend, helper, boot files, trust cache, device tree, boot manifest, graphics payload, guest tools, kernel and the verified base), guest_tools_sources (the guest tools built from the guest sources this checkout has), engine_patches (the engine built from this checkout's engine patches, from its build-manifest.json), saved_states (each saved state and the verified base still have their disks), last_run (the verdict ios.virtual.status shows as last_run), start_disk (whether the next start's disk copy fits, as the start refuses it), every ios.virtual.host_check item, gpu_now (the graphics card's free memory against the graphics memory guard's limit) and pressure_now (host I/O and memory pressure against the start's admission limits). ready is false when any item fails; status is the worst. Without a profile, profile fails and the machine's items still run. Reads files only, which takes some seconds for the kernel and payloads; starts and writes nothing.

No arguments.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.doctor
```

### ios.virtual.setup

Set up the virtual iOS device. writes, idempotent.

Walk the virtual iOS device's setup chain (docs/virtual-ios/setup.md) as one guided sequence. step plan (the default) reads which of the 17 stages are done from their outputs under work and the checkout's .tooling and writes nothing but work/inputs.json: stages lists each with stage, what, state (done, pending, partial when an earlier run stopped halfway, unknown when only the person can tell), detail, needs (arguments it still lacks), ask_first, why_ask, manual and the commands it would run; next is the first stage not done; inputs is tools/check_ios_inputs.py's check of the person's own files and host is ios.virtual.host_check. step run starts the next stage, or the one named by stage, as a durable job (or the operation it is, such as ios.emulator.prepare_userland) and returns it; a done stage is skipped without running anything. run refuses with ios_setup_out_of_order before an earlier stage is done, ios_setup_needs_input when the person's files are not given, ios_setup_inputs_invalid when they are the wrong ones, ios_setup_partial for a half-finished output (move it aside; nothing is deleted), ios_setup_confirm for stages that build for long or need the person's template until confirm is true, ios_setup_manual for the restore, which boots a guest and is run by hand from its commands, and ios_setup_needs_checkout for the engine without a source checkout. Nothing of Apple's is fetched: the restore images, decrypted, the public template and the IM4M stay the person's to supply.

- `work` string, required (non-empty): Absolute directory for the chain's outputs (boot, trees, storage, userland, cryptex, kernel, guest tools, profile); created by the first stage that writes there
- `step` string (one of plan, run; default "plan"): plan reports; run starts a stage
- `stage` string (one of engine, support, linker, gpu_plugin, boot, trees, manifest, userland, restore_runtime, restore, cryptex_first, guest_tools, cryptex, kernel, first_install, profile, configure): With run: the stage to start; by default the first that is not done
- `confirm` boolean (default false): With run: the person agreed to a stage that asks first
- `restored` boolean (default false): The restore finished with restore_completed:true, so the stages after it may run
- `iphone_firmware` string (non-empty): Absolute unpacked iPhone17,3 24A446 restore image
- `pcc_firmware` string (non-empty): Absolute unpacked PCC 23E5207q restore image
- `iphone_os_image` string (non-empty): Absolute decrypted iPhone OS image; by default found under decrypted/ in iphone_firmware
- `iphone_systemos_image` string (non-empty): Absolute decrypted iPhone SystemOS Cryptex image; by default found under decrypted/ in iphone_firmware
- `pcc_system_image` string (non-empty): Absolute decrypted PCC system image; by default found under decrypted/ in pcc_firmware
- `template` string (non-empty): Absolute public ticket.shsh2 research template, for the manifest stage
- `manifest` string (non-empty): Absolute IM4M; by default work/your.im4m, which the manifest stage makes
- `vphone_cli` string (non-empty): Absolute vphone-cli checkout at the pinned revision, for the GPU plugin
- `swift_lib` string (non-empty): Absolute Linux Swift toolchain's usr/lib/swift, for the linker
- `clang` string (non-empty): Absolute clang 22, for the guest tools
- `helper_kernel` string (non-empty): Absolute kernel for the disk-preparing helper; by default the support's apfs/vmlinuz, else the running kernel's
- `jobs` integer (1 to 64; default 8): Parallel build jobs for the engine and linker
- `cpu_optimization` string (one of portable, native; default "portable"): Engine build: portable, or native for this CPU only (what was measured)

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.setup '{"work":"<work>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.configure

Set up virtual iOS device. writes, idempotent.

Select the prepared profile directory used by ios.virtual.start and ios.virtual.stop. The directory must contain a format 1 profile.json (prepare and boot inputs, graphics bundle, engine, application, installs) and a state.json naming the last closed run. Both are validated; nothing is created or repaired. With model alone, the configured profile is kept and only the device model for the next start changes. add_application, remove_application and application change the profile's own app list and the app the start opens, in profile.json; clang names the clang 22 the start rebuilds guest tools with. With add_application and deploy, the app also goes onto the running phone at once (ios.virtual.deploy, in deploy_job). Choosing another directory is refused with ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs and with ios_virtual_running while the current profile's phone runs; each directory configured is remembered for ios.virtual.profiles.

- `directory` string (non-empty): Existing profile directory. Becomes the profile of the next start; refused while the current profile's phone runs or a start or stop is in progress.
- `model` string (matching ^[a-z0-9-]{0,32}$): Device model the next start describes the phone as (an id from ios.virtual.status models). Empty: the profile's own description, a phone with a Home button.…
- `add_application` string (non-empty): Host path of an .app directory built for arm64 iOS to add to the profile's applications. It is inspected first (Info.plist, arm64 executable, only allowlisted…
- `add_entitlements` string: Entitlements plist to request for add_application; empty: the executable's embedded entitlements, or only application-identifier.
- `remove_application` string (non-empty): Host path or bundle identifier of a listed app to remove from the profile. If it was the app the start opens, the owned diagnostic is opened again.
- `application` string (matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]{0,254}$): Bundle identifier of the app the start opens after boot: the owned diagnostic (io.github.marselnenaj.tomacco.research-app) or one of the listed applications.
- `clang` string: Host path of the clang 22 executable the start rebuilds guest tools with (profile.json toolchain.clang); empty removes it, so a clang-22 on PATH or the build's…
- `deploy` boolean (default false): With add_application: install it on the running phone now, without a reboot. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.
- `deploy_open_app` boolean (default true): With deploy: open the app afterwards.
- `start_disks` string (one of copy, overlay): How the next start makes its root disk (profile.json start_disks): overlay makes an empty qcow2 overlay on the base run's root disk with qemu-img (beside the…
- `stall_seconds` integer (30 to 86400): How long a running phone may show no new frame, console output or guest answer before ios.virtual.status calls it quiet, and, after a probe the guest service…

List the apps of the configured virtual iOS device in one place: the owned diagnostic, every app profile.json lists (bundle path, bundle_id, name, display_name, entitlements) with version, build and minimum_os read from its bundle's Info.plist on the host now (bundle_readable false with bundle_error when the bundle is gone; null when it could not be read at all; bundle_id_changed when the bundle now names another identifier), and any app the current run has installed that the profile no longer lists (listed false). installed and installed_cdhash are the current run's record of what a start or ios.virtual.deploy installed; they do not say whether the bundle changed since, which the next start checks itself. opens_at_start marks the app the start opens. ### ios.virtual.start

Start virtual iOS device. writes.

Start the configured virtual iOS device as one durable job: prepare a new private disk copy from the last cleanly closed run (reinstalling guest tools and restoring the Preboot Metal driver the guest removes), boot it, attempt passcode-free unlock with Home presses and request the configured app once the native screen-state query confirms unlock. Launch acceptance does not establish a visible application scene. A guest that is already running is adopted. Disks of a run that did not close with verified storage are never reused. Follow progress with ios.virtual.status and job.logs. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. A late screen-query receipt is followed by its original request ID. application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. A start that would make a disk copy is refused with ios_virtual_disk_space, before anything is deleted or copied, when the filesystem of the profile's installs lacks the base's disks plus 1 GiB, counting the older copies the start deletes first; a filesystem that clones files (reflink) needs only the 1 GiB. A start that boots a guest returns warnings, a list of {check, message}: check gpu when under a quarter of the graphics card is free (the graphics memory guard stops a session under an eighth), check pressure when the host's I/O or memory pressure is over the admission limits the start waits for; neither refuses the start. Refused with ios_virtual_host_too_small on a host that is not x86_64 or has less than 12 GiB of memory.

- `open_app` boolean (default true): False boots and waits for the guest service only.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.start
```

### ios.virtual.stop

Stop virtual iOS device. writes, idempotent.

Flush guest storage, stop the running virtual iOS device, wait for its final report and record whether its disks closed with exit 0 and complete storage hashes. Only such a run is used as the base of the next start.

No arguments.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.stop
```

### ios.virtual.unlock

Unlock virtual iOS device. writes, idempotent.

Leave the running virtual iOS device's lock screen the way a start does, as one short job: observe the native screen state, then wake the display and press Home (or swipe up on a model without a Home button) with the start's pacing until a fresh observation says it is unlocked. The job's screen is unlocked, or not-checked when the guest tools cannot report the screen (nothing is pressed then). A passcode is never entered: a lock screen with one, or one that stays locked for 10 minutes, fails the job. ios.virtual.deploy (before it opens the app) and testing.run on the virtual-iphone device unlock the same way first; testing.run fails with ios_virtual_locked when it cannot. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off and ios_virtual_busy during a start or stop.

No arguments.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.unlock
```

### ios.virtual.cleanup

Clean up virtual iOS device disk copies. **destructive, ask first**.

Delete older disk copies of the configured virtual iOS device from the profile's installs directory, or with dry_run (the default) only report what would go. Only copies the start recorded as its own (state.json created) that lie directly in installs and are named guest-install* are candidates; the verified base, the current run and a start's attempt are always kept (kept, with the reason). Each copy's files are locked before it is deleted, so a copy a running guest holds is refused with the reason. A guest-install* directory the state does not record is listed under unrecorded and never deleted. copies lists each candidate with path, bytes (allocated on disk; blocks a reflinked copy shares with its base are counted in full) and removed; reclaimable_bytes is their sum and freed_bytes what was deleted. A real cleanup is refused with ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs.

- `dry_run` boolean (default true): Only report; delete nothing. false deletes the candidates.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.cleanup
```

### ios.virtual.state_save

Save state of virtual iOS device. writes, idempotent.

Keep the last verified run of the configured virtual iOS device under a name, so a later start can begin from it with ios.virtual.state_use. Nothing is copied: a verified run's disks never change after its stop, and the start's pruning and ios.virtual.cleanup keep every saved run's disk copy and the copies its overlay reads. Refused with ios_virtual_no_verified_run when no run has been stopped cleanly, ios_virtual_state_exists for a name in use unless replace, and ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs. A running phone is fine: the saved run is the last verified one, not the running one.

- `name` string, required (matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{0,63}$): Name of the saved state: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit.
- `replace` boolean (default false): Point an existing name at the current verified run.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.state_save '{"name":"<name>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.state_delete

Delete saved state of virtual iOS device. **destructive, ask first**.

Remove a saved state's name and delete the disk copy it kept, when that copy is one the start made in the profile's installs and nothing else keeps it: not the verified base, the current run, a start's attempt, another saved state or a copy an overlay among those reads. kept_because says why a copy stayed; removed and freed_bytes what went. A copy a running guest holds is refused, not deleted. Refused with ios_virtual_state_unknown for an unknown name and ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs.

- `name` string, required (matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{0,63}$): Name of the saved state: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.state_delete '{"name":"<name>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.state_use

Start virtual iOS device from saved state. writes, idempotent.

Make a saved state the base of the next ios.virtual.start of the configured virtual iOS device: state.json then names its run as the verified run, and the start copies from it (or lays an overlay on it). The phone must be stopped (ios_virtual_running otherwise). When the current verified run has no saved name, a later start's pruning may delete its disks, so this is refused with ios_virtual_state_unsaved unless discard_current. Refused with ios_virtual_state_missing when the state's disks are gone and ios_virtual_busy while a start or stop runs. previous is the base it replaced.

- `name` string, required (matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{0,63}$): Name of the saved state: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit.
- `discard_current` boolean (default false): Give up the current verified run even though no saved state keeps it.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.state_use '{"name":"<name>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.deploy

Install app on running virtual iOS device. writes.

One step from a built .app directory to the app on the running phone, without a reboot: inspect the bundle, sign a copy ad hoc, exchange spare entries of this boot's trust cache for its hashes while the guest is stopped for a moment, send it over the guest channel, name it to the signing adapter, install it through installd and open it. A durable job: follow job.logs, whose deploy events carry each step's seconds. When this run installed the same signed app before (the cdhash of the ad hoc signed copy, which seals every file of the bundle), nothing is trusted, sent or installed: the deploy event unchanged follows signed and the app is only opened; force installs it again. The profile lists the app afterwards, so the next start stages it. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off: use ios.virtual.configure add_application and start it. A boot has 512 spare entries and the adapter's table of the boot takes 32 apps, frameworks and extensions.

- `bundle` string, required (non-empty): Host path of an .app directory built for arm64 iOS.
- `entitlements` string: Entitlements plist to request; empty: the executable's embedded entitlements, or only application-identifier.
- `open_app` boolean (default true): False installs without opening.
- `force` boolean (default false): Install even when this run has the same signed app installed already.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.deploy '{"bundle":"<bundle>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.debug

Debug process on virtual iOS device. writes.

Join lldb to one process of the running phone: a durable job holds a TCP port on the host's loopback and, once lldb connects, copies its bytes to /usr/libexec/debugserver in the guest, attached to the target. The first line of job.logs is an event with the port and the lldb command, process connect connect://127.0.0.1:<port>. The app needs get-task-allow (ios.virtual.deploy with such entitlements). One session per job; it ends when lldb disconnects. Anything that reaches this port controls that process, so it listens on loopback only.

- `target` string, required (matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$): The process's decimal PID or its name.
- `port` integer (0 to 65535; default 0): TCP port on 127.0.0.1; 0 picks a free one.
- `seconds` integer (10 to 86400; default 3600): Longest the session lasts.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.debug '{"target":"<target>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.crash_reports

Save crash reports of virtual iOS device. writes.

Read the running virtual iPhone's crash reports whose file names start with process (an app's executable name, or any report name prefix) through the guest service, as ios.emulator.guest crash_reports does, and keep each complete one as a file on the host at directory/<owner>/<name> (owner mobile or root). reports lists every match: owner, name, path, bytes, sha256, saved, and the pid, process, capture_time and incident_id parsed from its bytes; a report the guest could not read whole, or with a name or owner that is not a plain report name, has saved false, no path and the reason. Pass a saved path to ios.crash_symbolicate. The guest returns at most three reports per directory and 512 KiB of content in all, by descending file name, which is not crash time; collection_complete false means some were left out, and an empty list never proves that nothing crashed. Reports are never removed from the guest. Without directory, a new directory in Tomacco's data directory is used. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

- `process` string, required (non-empty, up to 255 characters): Report name prefix, usually the app's executable name
- `directory` string (default ""): Absolute host directory for the reports; created if missing. Empty: a new directory in Tomacco's data directory.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.crash_reports '{"process":"<process>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.syslog

Log of virtual iOS device. read-only, idempotent.

Read the configured virtual iPhone's log as structured lines: the guest's serial console (uart.log of its guest job, running or last), where the kernel prints and launchd forwards log records. Each line has offset (its byte offset), time (as the line gives it, or null), process (for a launchd record the service's last label part, for a UIKit application its executable-like last identifier part; kernel for a line of no known form), pid, service, sender (the forwarding subsystem or the library in name(library)[pid]), level (emergency, alert, critical, error, fault, warning, notice, info, debug, default, or null) and message (cut at 2000 characters). bundle_id keeps one app's lines, across relaunches, and the reply names its executable under app; refused with ios_virtual_application_unknown for an app the profile does not list. Without offset the last 256 KiB are read; pass next_offset back to follow the log. Only complete lines are returned; an unfinished one comes in a later read. more says a read stopped at max_lines or 1 MiB before the end; reset says an offset past the end (another run's log) started over at 0. job_id names the guest job read and running whether it still runs. Reads a host file; the guest is not asked. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when no run has a guest job and ios_virtual_log_unavailable before the console log exists.

- `process` string (up to 128 characters; default ""): Only lines whose process or service contains this, ignoring case. Empty: all.
- `bundle_id` string (up to 255 characters; default ""): Only this app's lines: those of the process named after its executable (read from the bundle the profile lists) and launchd's lines about its service. By name…
- `levels` array of string (items one of emergency, alert, critical, error, fault, warning, notice, info, debug, default, none; up to 11 items): Only lines with one of these levels; none matches lines without a level, such as the kernel's. Empty or absent: all.
- `contains` string (up to 256 characters; default ""): Only lines whose message contains this text.
- `offset` integer (at least 0): Byte offset to read on from: a previous reply's next_offset. Absent: the last 256 KiB.
- `max_lines` integer (1 to 5000; default 500): The most lines returned in one reply.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.syslog
```

### ios.virtual.screenshot

Screenshot of virtual iOS device. writes.

Save the running virtual iPhone's current screen as a PNG at path, from the same frame ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer. frame none (default) keeps the picture as it is; rounded cuts the screen's corners round with the radius of the model the phone runs as (square for the Home-button phone) and makes outside them transparent; device also puts a plain black bezel around it, a drawing with rounded outer corners and no buttons, not a picture of the phone. The corner radius is the circular arc of the device catalogue's value, not Apple's continuous curve. MCP returns a PNG of up to 4 MiB inline. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

- `path` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of the PNG to write, ending in .png; an existing file is replaced.
- `frame` string (one of none, rounded, device; default "none"): none: the screen as it is; rounded: round, transparent corners; device: rounded screen inside a plain bezel.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.screenshot '{"path":"<path>"}'
```

### ios.virtual.record

Record virtual iOS device screen. writes.

Record the running virtual iPhone's screen for seconds into an H.264 MP4 at path, as a durable job: the frames ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer, polled fps times a second and encoded by ffmpeg as they come (ffmpeg must be installed). A frame that has not changed, or a poll slower than one frame, repeats the last picture, so the video lasts as long as the recording; the guest itself draws about 10 changed frames a second on this host. The job's result names the file and counts frames_written, frames_captured and frames_distinct; a phone that stops ends the recording early with what it has (ended_early). Follow it with job.wait and job.logs. job.send stop ends the recording early and keeps the video recorded so far (stopped_early). One recording at a time. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.

- `path` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of the MP4 to write, ending in .mp4; an existing file is replaced when the recording succeeds.
- `seconds` integer (1 to 600; default 10): How long to record.
- `fps` integer (1 to 30; default 10): Frames per second of the video, and how often a frame is asked for.

```sh
tomaccoctl call ios.virtual.record '{"path":"<path>"}'
```
